hook: The man with sport's longest winning streak has a sad story behind it.
story: The sport is squash: two players sealed in a walled court, hitting the same ball off the front wall until one of them breaks. Jahangir Khan of Pakistan was world champion at seventeen, the youngest ever. Then, from 1981 to 1986, he simply did not lose: 555 consecutive matches, the longest winning streak in professional sport, per Guinness. He once won a professional final without conceding a single point.
number: Ten consecutive British Opens. Six World Opens. For half a decade, the entire professional tour was competing for second place.
closer: And the sad story? In November 1979, at a tournament in Adelaide, his older brother Torsam, a professional player himself, collapsed in the middle of a match and died. Jahangir was fifteen. He considered leaving the sport. Instead, he decided his career would be a tribute to his brother. All 555 wins were Torsam's too.
full_text: The man with sport's longest winning streak has a sad story behind it. The sport is squash: two players sealed in a walled court, hitting the same ball off the front wall until one of them breaks. Jahangir Khan of Pakistan was world champion at seventeen, the youngest ever. Then, from 1981 to 1986, he simply did not lose: 555 consecutive matches, the longest winning streak in professional sport, per Guinness. He once won a professional final without conceding a single point. Ten consecutive British Opens. Six World Opens. For half a decade, the entire professional tour was competing for second place. And the sad story? In November 1979, at a tournament in Adelaide, his older brother Torsam, a professional player himself, collapsed in the middle of a match and died. Jahangir was fifteen. He considered leaving the sport. Instead, he decided his career would be a tribute to his brother. All 555 wins were Torsam's too.
